- When sentiment is predominantly bullish (≥ 1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% if recent price drop is steep.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline, reduce forecast 5–10% in next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 50% of historical mean), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–7% for next 5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 3–8% in early periods; apply +3% bias to first 5–7 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lag correction to forecast (i.e., shift down 1–2 days in price trajectory).
